I gated `send_receipt` in `services/notifier/notifier/email.py` behind the `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_EMAIL` environment variable. The two tests pass.

- **Flag name:** the notifier is deployed separately and can't read the root `flags.toml`. Following the project's notifier flag convention, the flag is an environment variable, and `"1"` turns it on.
- **Off by default:** when the variable is unset or anything other than `"1"`, `send_receipt` returns `None` and sends nothing. Turn it on per environment by setting `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_EMAIL=1`.
- **Tests:** I updated the existing receipt test to set the flag and added one asserting nothing is sent when it's off.
- **Not a percentage rollout:** the convention only supports on/off per deployment, so "gradual" means enabling environment by environment. A percentage-based rollout would need a different mechanism, so tell me if you want that.
- **"New" receipt email:** `send_receipt` already existed and I found no separate new template, so I gated that function. If you meant a different or upcoming receipt email, point me to it.
- **Callers:** nothing else in the repo calls `send_receipt`, so callers that expect a message id from the old code will now get `None` when the flag is off.
